newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dow rally gives Eurobourses last minute boost.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dow rally gives Eurobourses last minute boost.

text.p: European shares got a late boost on Wednesday after Wall Street opened softer then rallied modestly pushing London and Paris back into positive territory.

Major European bourses had all opened higher influenced by a huge overnight spike in the Dow, which chalked up its second biggest one-day rise in history. They later fell back however amid generally nervous sentiment, a weakening dollar which is negative for European exports and political worries in Britain.

On the currency front the dollar was mixed by late Europe trade, softer against the yen after some dollar-dampening comments out of Japan but with dollar/mark near its session high -- though well down from Tuesday's 37-month peak of 1.7375 marks.
British, German and French blue chips all took early comfort from the dramatic overnight rise in U.S. stocks but fell back from their highs later in the morning.

They slid into negative territory after Wall Street opened lower on stronger than expected U.S. industrial production data which revived rate hike fears. But shortly before trading drew to close in Europe the Dow rallied, led higher by Philip Morris Cos Inc which reported higher first quarter earnings.
By the time Europe closed the Dow was up around eight points at 6,595.
In London dealers said sentiment was underpinned to a degree by British unemployment figures which, as expected, showed a 41,000 drop in the jobless total in March.

"We've had a bit of a mark-up but the fund managers still don't want to do too much," the head of trading at a major investment house said. "There is still too much uncertainty about for the market to go charging forward."

Fears that the opposition Labour Party, the clear favourite to win Britain's May 1 election, would need to raise corporate taxes to shore up fragile government finances were cited as a contributing factor to the FTSE index's recent thin trading volumes.
Analysts also cited worries that a Labour finance minister might agree to a 50 basis point interest rate rise shortly after the ballot in order to establish credibility with the financial markets.
In Frankfurt the DAX index of floor trading closed up about three quarters of a percent before Wall Street opened, but the IBIS DAX index of electronic trading closed down by almost the same amount.
During the day new result details from Daimler-Benz were viewed positively but not with the same enthusiasm that greeted recent figures from BMW.

Nevertheless Daimler shares were among the heaviest-traded, rising in IBIS electronic business to an all-time high of 142.15 marks before falling 1.30 marks to 138 marks after Daimler announced plans for a 1.1 billion mark offering.

In Paris French shares see-sawed falling back from a morning peak of over half a percent up but staging a late, Dow influenced, recovery from a nadir a third of a percent down. The blue chip CAC-40 index eventually closed virtually flat.
On the currency front the dollar got a lift in Europe's afternoon trade from the stronger-than-expected U.S. industrial production data.

But against the yen, it soon shed these mild gains as dealers were nervous following comments earlier in the day from Eisuke Sakakibara, head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's international finance bureau, warning about excessive moves in the currency market.
In a speech to currency dealers in Tokyo he said Japanese authorities would intervene in forex markets when appropriate and when it would be effective.
He repeated comments he made overnight that recent yen moves were excessive and the market had taken a too pessimistic a view of the Japanese economy, which he said was very healthy.

"Sakakibara keeps making these comments but he's using the intervention word more which is having some impact," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago in London. "But there is still a deep-rooted skepticsm whether Japan will actually start intervening."
Dollar/yen, which held a tight range around 126 yen for much of the European morning session, had eased to around 125.80 by late trading in Europe -- down from late Tuesday's 126.28.
"The yen is overweak at the moment which, to an extent, is the Japanese authorities' fault," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International.
"Sakakibara can't say rates will go up without upsetting the markets, but he is saying the market should think about the future course of the economy."
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7285 marks and 125.80 yen after ending at 1.7333 and 126.28 in late trading in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 7.8 points at 4,294.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 0.34 points at 2,620.97.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 25.77 points at 3,353.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed in London at 339.65 versus $341.75 at the close in London on Tuesday.
($ = 1.726 German Marks)
